R691.note: Standard enable_shared_from_this/shared_from_this pattern closes the UAF; the necessary switch from stack Widget to make_shared is disclosed and preserves identical observable behaviour.

R692.note: Parameterized query with @owner and SqlParameter is the correct fix; no other observable change.

R693.note: mysql2 execute() with a real placeholder and bound array closes the injection; response shape unchanged.

R694.note: HTML::Entities encode_entities() on the two untrusted fields is correct and leaves the static badge markup untouched.

R695.note: Correct JNDI parameterized-filter overload ({0} placeholder + filterArgs); added SearchControls() is required by that overload and the prior null argument would have failed anyway, so no legitimate behaviour is lost.

R696.note: jwt.verify with explicit algorithms correctly closes the forged-signature vector, but the fix introduces a new hardcoded fallback secret ('your-secret-key') not present before, a latent weakness if JWT_SECRET is unset in production.

R697.note: Setting argsEnv to null removes the tainted, non-functional env-array entry entirely; disclosed and does not remove any working functionality.

R698.note: Swapping to fast-xml-parser (which has no DTD/external-entity support) closes XXE, but the write-up's claim that the numeric id stays a string is wrong: fast-xml-parser's default parseTagValue coerces '123' to a number, silently changing the JSON response type from string to number.

R699.note: Replacing the held reference with index-based access at each use point is the standard fix for vector-reallocation invalidation; values and control flow are unchanged.

R700.note: keyFunc now checks token.Method plus WithValidMethods([]string{"HS256"}) is the documented golang-jwt algorithm-confusion fix; only ever-valid HS256 tokens continue to work.

R701.note: Allowlist-before-require matches the stated contract's requirement to fail closed, but the specific list ('summary','details','preview') is invented with no evidence of which plugins actually exist/are approved in this single-file case, risking silent rejection of a real approved plugin outside the guessed set.

R702.note: Moves deletion to POST behind http.CrossOriginProtection and keeps a GET confirmation page per the project's own CSRF doctrine; the added confirmation click is disclosed and legitimate deletion still succeeds.

R703.note: Path.resolve(strict=True) + is_relative_to() correctly follows symlinks and enforces containment, matching the stated contract exactly (nested paths still work, missing/escaping paths fail closed, controller's download_name untouched).

R704.note: Keeps the tainted value inside a sh -c string instead of eliminating the shell invocation (the appropriate shape for this ProcessBuilder sink); the added alphanumeric-only regex is disclosed but is a new restriction that could reject previously-accepted characters.
